t: Video Stitching — Minimum Clips to Cover [0, time]
o: We must pick the fewest clips whose union covers every point in $[0, time]$. This is a classic interval covering problem. In Example 1, sorting clips by start and greedily extending reach gives [0,2] → [1,9] (reach 9) → [8,10] (reach 10), so 3 clips. Example 2 fails because no clip starts at 0, leaving a gap at time 0, hence -1. Constraints are tiny ($n, time \le 100$), so even an $O(n^2)$ DP is fine, but a greedy sweep achieves $O(n \log n)$ or even $O(n + time)$.
k: Sort clips by start time; greedily pick, among clips starting within current coverage, the one reaching farthest.
If at any step no clip starts at or before the current covered end, coverage has a gap — return -1.
The problem reduces to 'minimum jumps to reach time' where each clip is a jump from start to end.

a.i: Let dp[t] be the minimum clips needed to cover [0, t]. For each t from 0 to time, try every clip that could end at t: if its start s satisfies dp[s] is finite, then dp[t] = min(dp[t], dp[s] + 1). This works because any optimal cover of [0,t] can be split into a cover of [0,s] plus this last clip.
s: Initialize dp[0] = 0 and dp[t] = infinity for t > 0.
For each t in 1..time, for each clip [s, e] with s < t <= e, set dp[t] = min(dp[t], dp[s] + 1).
a.t: O(n * time) — for each of time positions we scan all n clips.

a.i: Sort clips by start time. Sweep through them maintaining the farthest end reachable with the clips chosen so far; whenever we pass the boundary of the current chosen clip's end, we must take one more clip — pick the one reaching farthest. This greedy exchange argument holds because replacing any chosen clip with one that starts no later and ends no later-or-farther never hurts.
s: Track curEnd (end of last chosen clip), farthest (best reach among candidates), and count.
Iterate clips: if clip.start > curEnd, we need to commit the best candidate: increment count, set curEnd = farthest; if clip.start > curEnd still, return -1.
Update farthest = max(farthest, clip.end); when curEnd >= time, stop early.
After the loop, commit the final candidate and check curEnd >= time.
a.t: O(n log n) — sorting dominates; the sweep is O(n).
a.sp: O(1) extra space beyond sorting (or O(n) depending on sort implementation).

w: In an interview, lead with the greedy: it mirrors 'Jump Game II' and is the expected optimal answer; mention the DP as a simpler-to-reason alternative given tiny constraints. Pitfalls: forgetting the gap check (no clip starts at/before curEnd → -1), off-by-one on whether a clip ending exactly at curEnd counts as covering (it does, intervals are closed), and clips entirely outside [0, time]. Edge cases: time = 0 should return 0; a single clip [0, time] returns 1. Follow-ups: what if clips have costs (weighted interval cover → DP), or if you must report which clips were used (track parent pointers in DP or record chosen indices in greedy).
